primary_question: For the same frozen tasks and model snapshots, does producing a correct, maintainable workflow in .program change functional success or generation cost compared with Bash and Nushell?

development.purpose: Tune the evaluator and instructions. Never included in confirmatory results.

calibration.purpose: Freeze runner images, prompts, test oracles, scoring and model settings before held-out generation.

held_out.purpose: Confirmatory evaluation. Keep prompt bodies and oracle bundles sealed until all candidate artifacts are submitted.

holdout_rules: Assign a task family wholly to one split; no family, scenario seed, oracle, prompt, or material variant may cross splits.
Hash and timestamp the sealed task package, prompts, hidden oracles, and container images before the first model call.
Authors of candidate-language instructions and model operators must not see held-out task bodies or oracle contents before generation is locked.
Use identical task requirements, available reference material, tool access, time limits, and repair-feedback policy for each language arm.
Randomize arm order within task and model block; use a fresh conversation for every task, language, model snapshot, and replicate.
Run each arm with the same model snapshot and supported decoding parameters. Record unavailable or provider-default parameters explicitly; do not infer them.

For desktop_composition tasks, each workflow language is paired with the same declared QML/Quickshell target and acceptance criteria. QML-only rendering work is not treated as a Bash or Nushell equivalent. Do not score this stratum until a real supported runner exists.
Infrastructure errors are retained as a separate outcome. Exclusions and reruns must follow a rule written here before unblinding and retain the original record.

trial_policy.repair_feedback: A fixed, language-neutral summary of compiler/runtime/oracle criterion failures; never reveal hidden test inputs, expected values, or source oracle text.
required_record_fields: temperature, top_p, seed, token limits, and tool configuration (or explicit unavailable/default values)
provider-reported input, output, cached and reasoning tokens where available
provider-reported billed cost, currency, and whether it is measured or estimated
generation time, execution/test time, repair count, every attempt's artifact hash and outcome

scoring.primary_outcome: A task-arm trial succeeds only when every roster-declared mandatory black-box criterion passes on the final artifact within the fixed attempt budget.
secondary_outcomes: reported input/output/reasoning tokens and total tokens
provider-reported billed cost; price-sheet estimates remain separately labeled
blinded maintainability rubric scores from two independent raters
desktop visual and lifecycle criteria for the paired workflow+QML stratum
scoring.human_rubric: The exact rubric is benchmarks/ai_productivity/rubric.json with the recorded SHA-256 above. Two blinded raters score each submitted artifact independently on requirement coverage, clarity, and changeability. If any dimension differs, a third blinded rater scores all dimensions; preserve all scores and use the third rater as adjudicator.
scoring.claim_rule: Report each outcome and uncertainty separately. Do not claim general AI superiority from one task, one model, development/calibration data, unpaired summaries, or fixture tests. Any confirmatory language must name task strata, model snapshots, sample counts, and paired uncertainty.

analysis.unit: task-family cluster within a matched model-snapshot and replicate block
analysis.primary_comparison: Paired held-out final-success difference for execute_program versus each shell comparator on the same task family and model block.
analysis.uncertainty: Family-cluster paired bootstrap, 10000 resamples with fixed seed 20261014; show interval and raw paired counts. Treat the two comparator contrasts as a family and use 97.5% intervals (Bonferroni) for confirmatory wording.
analysis.efficiency: Report paired differences in cumulative reported tokens, provider-reported cost, repairs, and generation time. Do not replace failures with zero cost or report cost estimates as billed cost.
analysis.missingness: Keep provider refusal, timeout, invalid artifact, infrastructure failure, and missing usage as distinct states. No silent pairwise deletion.
